Good evening. I'm {anchor}, alongside {anchor2}. Tonight: {pop} dwarves, one fortress, and absolutely no shortage of opinions.
This is DNN. I'm {anchor}. If you're watching this instead of hauling stone, your overseer already knows.
From the deepest studio in {world}, this is DNN. I'm {anchor}, and yes, the cat is on the desk again.
Good evening, {fort}. It's {month} of {year}, and I'm {anchor}. Let's get to the headlines before someone throws a tantrum.
I'm {anchor}, {anchor2} is beside me, and this is the most trusted name in news carved out of solid rock.
This is DNN Tonight. I'm {anchor}. Our top story: everything, all at once, as usual.
Good evening and welcome to DNN. I'm {anchor}. We are coming to you live, mostly because we cannot afford to tape anything.

This is DNN. I'm {anchor}. Spring has arrived, the farmers are planting, and the elves are presumably hugging something.
Good evening. It's summer in {fort}, I'm {anchor}, and somewhere up there the sun is doing whatever it does.
This is DNN. I'm {anchor}. Autumn is here, the caravans are coming, and the bookkeeper is sweating.
Good evening. I'm {anchor}. It's been a quiet stretch in {fort}, which is exactly when DNN gets nervous.
Good evening, I'm {anchor}. Our cat-to-dwarf ratio has once again broken the record, and we'll have more on that later.
Tonight on DNN: hunger, hope, and a very long look at the empty larder. I'm {anchor}. Good evening.
This is DNN, and I'm {anchor}. Joining me as always, {anchor2}, who insists on being called senior co-anchor.
Good evening. I'm {anchor}. Our top story tonight was supposed to be something else, but then {citizen} happened.
This is DNN. I'm {anchor}. We are told the forge is hot, the depot is busy, and the noble is unhappy. So, a normal day.
Welcome back to another hour of DNN. I'm {anchor}. Tonight we go deeper than any network has gone. Literally. We dug.
Good evening, {fort}. I'm {anchor}. We remind viewers that the screen is not a drinking vessel. Please stop trying.

Good evening. I'm {anchor}. Before we begin, {citizen} would like everyone to know they did not take the last plump helmet.
From the studio to your stockpile, this is DNN. I'm {anchor}, and tonight the news is heavy enough to need a wheelbarrow.

close.text: That's all for tonight. I'm {anchor}. Drink responsibly, haul diligently, and never trust an elf. Good night, {fort}.
For {anchor2} and the whole DNN crew, I'm {anchor}. Good night, and mind the magma.
That's the news. I'm {anchor}. Go to bed, all {pop} of you. Yes, you too, {citizen}.
And that's DNN for this evening. Whatever happens tonight, we'll be here to overreact to it tomorrow.
I'm {anchor}. Thank you for watching DNN. Please return your mugs to the tavern on the way out.
That's our broadcast. Remember: a fortress is only as strong as its ale supply. Good night from DNN.
From all of us at DNN, good night. And to whoever keeps moving the studio chairs: we know. We know.
That's it for this hour. I'm {anchor}. Stay safe, stay sober-ish, and stay away from the cistern.
Good night, {fort}. This has been DNN. If you see something strange in the caverns, see it from far away.
I'm {anchor}, signing off. May your barrels be full and your moods be mild.
And so ends another day in {fort}. I'm {anchor}, this was DNN, and the cat is still on the desk.
That's the news for {month}. I'm {anchor}. Sleep well, wake early, and dig straight down only with permission.
This has been DNN. I'm {anchor}. Tomorrow: more news, probably the same news, but louder.
Good night from DNN. A reminder that the hospital is for the injured, not for napping. Looking at you, {citizen}.
For DNN, I'm {anchor}. Thank you for trusting us with your evenings. We'll try to deserve it.
That's all the time we have. {anchor2} and I will be in the tavern if anyone needs a quote.
I'm {anchor}. This was DNN. Remember, the news is just the stuff that happened while you were hauling.
Good night, {civ}. Good night, {fort}. And good night to the one dwarf still mining at this hour. Go home.
That wraps up tonight's DNN. Keep your picks sharp and your gossip sharper.
I'm {anchor}. We leave you tonight with the gentle sound of a dwarf arguing with a door. Good night.
Thank you for watching DNN. The year is {year}, the fortress stands, and that is plenty.
This has been DNN. Stay warm out there, and by out there we mean in here. Nobody go outside.
Good night from DNN. The rain continues on the surface. Our reporter is still standing in it. We'll check on them tomorrow.
That's DNN for tonight. The barrels are low, so if you've been hiding a cask, now is the time to share. Good night.
I'm {anchor}. It was a hard day in {fort}. Hold your friends close tonight. Good night.
That's our show. It was a quiet day, which, as every dwarf knows, means something is coming. Sleep lightly.
Good night from DNN. To the newest arrivals of {fort}: welcome. Your bedroom is probably a hallway for now.
This has been DNN. After all these years, {fort} still stands, and so does this desk, barely. Good night.
I'm {anchor}. Good night to all {pop} viewers. We counted. It took a while.
That's all for DNN tonight. With food running short, we ask you to dream of roasts. Good night.
For {anchor2}, for the crew, and for the cats who outnumber us all, good night from DNN.
I'm {anchor}, and that's the way it is, deep beneath {world}. Good night.
That's the broadcast. If you have a news tip, leave it at the depot. If you have ale, leave it with us.
Good night from DNN. Remember: every masterpiece starts as a dwarf staring at a workshop and refusing to explain.
I'm {anchor}. Thanks for watching. This has been DNN, and the stone will still be here in the morning.

banter.a: {anchor2}, did you see the dining hall this morning?
banter.b: I did. Someone carved a masterwork table and then ate off the floor anyway.

banter.a: I'm told the tavern has a new drink.
banter.b: It's the same drink, {anchor}. They just put it in a different barrel.

banter.a: {anchor2}, any plans for the weekend?
banter.b: Dwarves don't have weekends, {anchor}. I'll be hauling stone and crying quietly.

banter.a: I see a cat has joined us on the desk again.
banter.b: That's not a cat, that's management.

banter.a: {anchor2}, have you been to the new hospital wing?
banter.b: I have. Lovely beds. Shame about the screaming.

banter.a: How's your beard, {anchor2}?
banter.b: Majestic. Thank you for asking. Nobody ever asks.

banter.a: Did you hear {citizen} tried to befriend an elf caravan?
banter.b: I heard. {citizen} now has a wooden mug and a deep sense of regret.

banter.a: {anchor2}, would you ever take a strange mood?
banter.b: If I did, you'd be the first dwarf I'd demand bones from.

banter.a: I see we've had migrants again.
banter.b: Wonderful. More dwarves to sleep in the corridors.

banter.a: {anchor2}, what's your favourite stone?
banter.b: Microcline. Don't make me say why on live television.

banter.a: The noble issued another mandate today.
banter.b: Let me guess. Something we've never heard of, made of something we don't have.

banter.a: Have you tried the plump helmet roast?
banter.b: Tried it, loved it, wrote it a short poem.

banter.a: {anchor2}, the ale supply is looking thin.
banter.b: I've noticed. My hands have noticed. My whole personality has noticed.

banter.a: Big stockpile of ale this season.
banter.b: Best news we've reported all year, and I include the artifact.

banter.a: I think the carp in the river are getting bolder.
banter.b: I think the carp in the river have always been bold. We just got softer.

banter.a: {anchor2}, you seem quiet tonight.
banter.b: I'm saving my energy for the crossfire segment. Someone's going to say something wrong.

banter.a: How many cats do we have now?
banter.b: Too many to count and too few to stop.

banter.a: {anchor2}, quick question: who let the goat in the studio?
banter.b: That's my goat. Next question.

banter.a: I heard {citizen} and {citizen2} had a falling-out.
banter.b: Over a sock. A single sock. It was a very good sock.

banter.a: Do you ever think about the surface?
banter.b: Once. Then I had a lie down.

banter.a: {anchor2}, it's raining on the surface.
banter.b: Good. Let it rain. We have roofs, and the roofs are mountains.

banter.a: Snow again up top.
banter.b: I'll put it in my diary, right under 'Did not go outside.'

banter.a: {anchor2}, you were late to the desk today.
banter.b: I was stuck behind a dwarf carrying one pebble very slowly.

banter.a: Lovely craftsmanship on your mug.
banter.b: Thank you. It's decorated with an image of the mug itself.

banter.a: Any word from the mountainhome?
banter.b: Only that they love us and would like more taxes.

banter.a: {anchor2}, have you seen the new engraving in the hallway?
banter.b: Yes, it's a picture of a dwarf looking at an engraving. Very meta.

banter.a: It was a tough day for the fortress.
banter.b: It was. Let's be gentle with each other tonight.

banter.a: Nothing has gone wrong all week.
banter.b: Please stop saying that out loud.

banter.a: I'm told the depot is busy today.
banter.b: Every caravan wants our crafts and nobody wants our opinions.

banter.a: {anchor2}, if you were an animal, what would you be?
banter.b: A cat, obviously. Sleep on things, ignore nobles, get fed.

banter.a: Have you visited the temple lately?
banter.b: I went to pray. Mostly I napped. The gods understand.

banter.a: How's the food situation?
banter.b: Let's just say I'm eyeing the studio cat with new interest.

banter.a: The larder is overflowing.
banter.b: That's what I like to hear. Eat a roast, be a roast.

banter.a: {anchor2}, did you get your new bedroom?
banter.b: I did. It's a beautiful room with no door, no bed, and a lot of rock.

banter.a: Another baby was born this week.
banter.b: That makes the dining hall even louder. Congratulations to all, apologies to my ears.

banter.a: Do you think the elves watch DNN?
banter.b: I hope so. I hope they're very upset.

banter.a: {anchor2}, what do you think of the new militia captain?
banter.b: Very brave. Shouts a lot. Mostly at doors.

banter.a: The miners struck a new vein of ore.
banter.b: And by struck, they mean they tripped on it.

banter.a: We are so small a fortress right now.
banter.b: Cosy, {anchor}. The word you're looking for is cosy.

banter.a: This fortress is enormous now.
banter.b: I passed a dwarf in the hall today I have never seen in my life.

banter.a: {anchor2}, spring has arrived.
banter.b: I'll mark the occasion by staying exactly where I am.

banter.a: Hot one up top this summer.
banter.b: I'll take your word for it. I've never seen the sun and I'm proud of it.

banter.a: Leaves are falling on the surface.
banter.b: The elves must be devastated. Lovely.

banter.a: It's winter again, {anchor2}.
banter.b: Good. The rivers freeze, the carp sleep, and I finally relax.

banter.a: Do you ever dream about magma, {anchor2}?
banter.b: Every night. It's warm, it's orange, and it never asks me to do paperwork.

banter.a: I heard the bookkeeper is behind.
banter.b: The bookkeeper is always behind. That's what makes them a bookkeeper.

banter.a: {anchor2}, the mayor wants an interview.
banter.b: Tell them we're busy. Tell them we've always been busy.

banter.a: How old do you think this fortress is now?
banter.b: Old enough to have a haunted hallway, young enough to argue about it.

banter.a: We barely have walls yet.
banter.b: Walls are a state of mind, {anchor}.

banter.a: I saw {citizen} sparring in the barracks today.
banter.b: {citizen} lost to a training dummy. The dummy has filed a complaint.

banter.a: {anchor2}, you have something on your beard.
banter.b: That's dinner. I'm saving it for later.

banter.a: Did anyone clean the studio?
banter.b: I'm told the cats did, in their own way.

banter.a: {anchor2}, what's the most dwarven thing you did today?
banter.b: Drank, dug, argued, drank again. A perfect circle.

banter.a: I've been told there's a forgotten beast in the caverns.
banter.b: Then I suggest we continue to forget it.

banter.a: They're building a new statue in the hall.
banter.b: Let me guess. It's of the noble, and the noble paid for it with our socks.

banter.a: The engravers did a portrait of you, {anchor}.
banter.b: It's very flattering. You're surrounded by cheese.

banter.a: Did {citizen2} really drink an entire barrel?
banter.b: Allegedly. DNN cannot confirm, but the barrel is empty and {citizen2} is singing.

banter.a: I think the newsroom needs a door.
banter.b: Doors are for fortresses with secrets, {anchor}. We are journalists.

banter.a: Our ratings are up this week.
banter.b: That's because the tavern screen is the only lit thing in the room.

banter.a: {anchor2}, any final thoughts before the break?
banter.b: Yes. Check on your friends, hug a cat, and hide the good ale.

Still to come: a look back at how {fort} grew to {pop} dwarves, and where we put them all.
Coming up: a fortress of just {pop}. We meet every single one of them. Well, most.
After the break: a quiet week in {fort}. Our pundits say it's the calm before the storm.
Still ahead: remembering a friend, and the stories they left behind.
Coming up: the ins and outs of the dining hall seating plan. It's political.
After the break: how to tell if a dwarf is in a mood, and how to run away politely.
Stay with us for more from {fort}, including the story everyone's whispering about.
Coming up: the militia trains hard, and the training dummies take it personally.
After the break: the mysterious hallway noise. Is it a ghost, a cat, or {citizen}?

markets.text: And now, the markets. Let's see how the stockpiles are doing, and whether to panic.
Time for the Ale Index, the only number in {fort} that truly matters.
Let's check in on the stockpile markets. Brace your mugs.
Now to business. Here are today's numbers from the fortress stockpiles.
Turning to the markets: the barrels have spoken, and they have opinions.
Our markets desk has been counting all day. Let's see what they found.
And now the markets report. Viewers with weak hearts may want to look away.
Time for the markets, and good news for once: the barrels are full.
Let's look at the larder. It's grim. We're doing it anyway.
Now, the market numbers. Cat futures continue to soar.
Here's the stockpile report, brought to you by the dwarves who actually haul things.
On to the markets, where every gem, bar and barrel is counted, twice, by a nervous bookkeeper.

weather.text: Let's check the weather on the surface, not that any of us are going up there.
Now to the weather desk, where it's {weather} up top and stone down here.
Time for the weather. It's {weather} outside. Inside, it's a perfect fortress day.
And now the forecast for the surface, a place known for its unpredictable sky.
Let's see what the sky is doing. The sky, for our younger viewers, is the big ceiling outside.
Here's the weather. Farmers and woodcutters, listen up. Everyone else, carry on drinking.
It's raining on the surface, so let's go to the weather desk for the soggy details.
Snow on the surface again. Here's the weather desk to tell us how much we won't be shovelling.
Clear skies up top. Let's go to the weather desk, who is suspicious of it.
Winter has a grip on the surface. Here's the forecast.
Summer weather update now, for anyone foolish enough to stand in the sun.
And now the weather, for the three dwarves who actually go outside.

sports.text: Now to sports, where the sparring ring has been busy and the hospital busier.
Time for the sports desk. Wrestling, dodging, and competitive hauling, all ahead.
Let's go to sports. Tonight, the barracks have something to prove.
And now the sports report. Who's punching whom in {fort} this week?
It's sports time. Grab a mug and pick a side.
Turning to the sports desk, where the training dummies are once again undefeated.
Now the sports roundup. The hauling league standings have shifted dramatically.
Here's sports. Remember, in the sparring ring, everyone is a champion until they are not.
Let's check the sports news, sponsored by the bonesetter.
On to sports. Our sports desk has been waiting all day and has already had three ales.
Sports now. A quiet week means more time for training, and more time for bragging.
And now to the sports desk, where the {season} season is in full swing.

world.text: Let's turn to the world desk for news from beyond the mountain.
Now, the world. What are the elves, goblins and humans up to? Nothing good, presumably.
Time for world news. Here's what's happening in {world} while we were busy digging.
And now our world desk, with news from {civ} and everyone else.
Let's look abroad. Our world correspondent has spoken to some caravan guards.
Here's the world report, bringing you news from places you'll never visit.
Now to international news, by which we mean anything above the cavern layer.
Let's check on the wider world. The mountainhome sends its regards and its demands.
On to world news. Our sources in {world} have been gossiping again.
The world desk now, where the goblins continue to be goblins.
Let's go to the world desk. The elves have, once again, done something with trees.
And now, news from across {world}, filtered through several rumours and one very tired messenger.

trade.text: Now to the trade desk, where the depot is open for business.
Time for trade news. The caravan from {caravan_civ} has arrived, and it wants our mugs.
Let's go to the trade desk. Did we get a good deal? Our broker says yes. Our broker always says yes.
And now trade. Here's what's moving through the depot this season.
Trade desk time. Who's buying, who's selling, and who's being ripped off.
Let's check the depot. Our trade reporter is standing between two very large wagons.
Here's the trade report. Elves, please note: no, we will not stop using wood.
Turning to the trade desk, where haggling is considered a contact sport.
The caravan season is upon us. Here's the trade desk.
On to trade, where {caravan_civ} has some strong feelings about our prices.
Let's see what the merchants brought, and what they took home.
Now for the trade numbers, presented by a bookkeeper who would like a raise.

works.text: Now to the works desk, where the biggest project in {fort} continues to take shape.
Time for the works report. How's {project} coming along? Let's find out.
Let's check in on the construction crews. It's a big job and they have big opinions.
And now the works desk, with updates on {project} and the dwarves building it.
Here's the works report. Hard hats on, viewers.
On to construction news. The masons have been busy, and the haulers have been complaining.

The works desk now, where {project} is either nearly done or never going to be. Let's ask.
Time to check the building sites. Our works reporter is covered in dust and proud of it.
Construction update: the fortress is growing, block by block.
Here's the works desk. In a fortress this old, there's always something to fix.
Let's go to the works desk for news on {project}, the talk of the dining hall.

crossfire.text: Time for Crossfire, where two pundits argue loudly about things that may not matter.
And now Crossfire. Two dwarves, one desk, no agreement. Let's begin.

Now Crossfire, the segment that's ruined more friendships than the tavern.

Time for Crossfire, where the facts are optional and the volume is mandatory.
Let's turn to our panel for Crossfire. They are already arguing. Let's join them.
Crossfire now. Things are peaceful in {fort}, so our pundits will invent conflict.

interview.text: Now we go live to an interview with one of the hard-working dwarves of {fort}.
Let's hear from an ordinary dwarf. We find them more interesting than nobles.
Time for our street interview. Well, corridor interview.
Let's go live to our reporter, who has stopped a citizen to ask a few questions.

We go now to an interview with a dwarf who did not ask to be on television.

Time for DNN Asks, where we ask a dwarf what they think and they tell us.

Let's hear what an everyday dwarf thinks about life in {fort}.
We've caught a dwarf between jobs. Let's go live before they get away.
